text:
incident_bot: ALERT: runtime-prod-us-west-1 high restart rate (pods: model-server-*). Autoscaler activity detected. Severity: P1-ish. Pager: https://pager.redwood/INC-2795. Notified on-call.

devon: ack — I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking node events.

devon: quick snapshot from logs:
```
E tensorflow: Allocation of 2147483648 bytes failed
E runtime: CUDA driver mismatch: expected 525.85, found 520.61
W kubelet: Container killed (OOMKilled)
```

maria: seeing same in runtime metrics — GPU mem utilization spikes to ~98% then pods crashloop. Looks correlated with an autoscale surge that added many small G4dn nodes then they start OOMing immediately.

ken: I think cluster-autoscaler bounce + workload burst = thrash. CA scaled to 30 nodes, then back down to 8 in ~5m. Pods kept landing on new nodes with slightly different driver kernels.

devon: timeline so far:
- 2794999940: autoscaler surge triggered (latency SLOs high)
- 2795000000: incident_bot page
- 2795000062: first OOMKILL observed in model-server-7f4c
- 2795000220: scale-up to 30 nodes complete
- 2795000400: mass pod restarts, CUDA driver mismatch logs
- 2795000800: CA started rapid scale-down

maria: customer impact: several customers routed through us-west saw 5xxs and degraded throughput. Support received multiple tickets (TKT-4891, TKT-4893). We have spike in error-rate dashboard: 5xx rate from 0.2% -> 4.7% for embeddings endpoints.

support-bot: Notified customers in affected orgs: acme-inc, beta-saas. Sent status update: "We are investigating a degradation in inference for US-WEST; temporary workarounds in progress."

ken: immediate mitigation options:
- pin scheduling to driver-compatible nodes (nodeSelector gpu.driver=525.85) and taint other nodes, OR
- temporarily disable CA scale-down (prevent rapid shrink), OR
- set maxSurge / maxUnavailable to avoid mass scheduling churn, OR
- roll back recent runtime image that introduced slightly different CUDA bindings.

maria: also can switch traffic to quantized-model-variant q8 to reduce memory pressure per request. That will lower perf slightly but reduce OOM risk.

devon: quick try: cordon some of the newer nodes to stop pod churn, and set CA cool-down to 10m. Doing now.

ops-bot: Command executed: `kubectl cordon n-g4dn-new-02` — success.

devon: changed cluster-autoscaler flag: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and `--scan-interval=30s`. Increased max-node-provision-time to 8m.

maria: deploy-bot: can we do a controlled canary to q8 variant?

deploy-bot: new canary deploy initiated -> route 10% traffic to model-server:q8-canary in us-west-1.

ken: also rolling back runtime image to 2026-02-14 build could remove driver mismatch. Anyone have objections?

maria: no objection, do canary first and monitor. If q8 reduces errors, expand. If not, rollback.

devon: observing drop in restart-rate after cordon + CA cooldown. Restart count per pod down from 7 -> 1 in last 10m. Good sign.

support-bot: Updated customers: "We have identified root cause as autoscaler-driven scheduling churn leading to CUDA mismatches and OOMs. Mitigation in progress: canary of lower-memory model and preventing scale-down. ETA next update in 15m."

lia: taking handoff in 20m. summary for next on-call: current state: canary at 10% q8, CA cooldown in effect, recent cordon applied to new nodes, investigating runtime image rollback if canary not stable. customer impact: intermittent 5xxs reduced but some customers still see errors. tickets TKT-4891/TKT-4893 open.

lia: a couple action items I want to own during handoff:
- validate GPU driver versions across nodepool (run `nvidia-smi --query` job)
- expand canary to 30% if 5xxs <1% for 10m
- coordinate with infra for a targeted node drain/replace if kernel-driver mismatch persists

devon: added temporary k8s node label `runtime-stable=true` on older pool and updated runtime DaemonSet tolerations so new pods prefer stable pool.

ken: note — downstream CI had a runtime image push earlier today that updated libcudnn minor. If we roll back, we should coordinate with model-onboarding to re-verify.

maria: metrics: embedding latency p95 increased from 180ms -> 420ms during surge, now down to ~210ms after mitigations. Error rate down to 1.1% overall (was 4.7%).

deploy-bot: canary at 10% q8 has shown 0 OOMs in the canary group for 12m.

lia: thanks. I'll pick this up. @devon please leave the CA cooldown and cordon in place until I confirm a stable window. I'll post updates every 15m.

devon: leaving CA tweak in place. also adding alert suppression rule for the noisy restart-alert to avoid paging during ongoing mitigation (incidents team aware).

incident_bot: NOTE: Pager cleared for now. Incident remains open. Next update scheduled at 2795000900.

lia: handoff complete. main outstanding risk: autoscaler policy needs tuning to avoid future rapid scale-up/down with this workload pattern. Raising a follow-up RFC for autoscale damping and heterogeneous node driver tagging.

ken: +1 on RFC. Also propose per-pool driver-version gating and preflight `nvidia-smi` job before scheduling new GPU workloads.

support-bot: Customer postmortem draft started: https://docs.redwood/incidents/INC-2795-draft. Please add notes on mitigation timeline and user impact.

lia: will update. closing handoff.

ops-bot: Incident status: in mitigation. Participants: devon, maria, ken, lia.

deploy-bot: Reminder: anything we roll back must go through canary before full rollout.

devon: thanks team. I'll stay around for another 30m and then unassign.

licit: (this is a quick note for the record) — we observed that bursty batching in the embeddings path caused large, sudden KV cache allocations which amplified memory usage per process. Need to tune batching heuristics and TTL caching policy.

maria: noted. adding to postmortem action items: batching smoothing + safe-quant fallback.

incident_bot: closed? not yet — status: monitoring.

-- end of thread --
